title: Intake Condition Step on the Dryer Rate for Wet and Light Grain
content:
Wet, light grain costs more to run, so the dryer rate carries a step under Grain Storage and Conditioning Agreements. The two readings that decide the step are the moisture and the test weight the scale recorded when the load was taken into store, which stand on the member's own scale ticket in the grain ledger kept under Grain Marketing Contracts.

## Clause

Where the scale read the grain in above the wet-intake moisture of 20.0 percent and weighed it in below the light-test weight of 54.0 pounds, the deep-dry step of 0.008 for each point on each bushel is added to the programme's rate.

Where the scale read the grain in above the wet-intake moisture and weighed it in at or above the light-test weight, the wet-corn step of 0.004 for each point on each bushel is added.

And otherwise, the scale having read the grain in at or below the wet-intake moisture, no step is added for the state the grain came in at.

## The combinations, with both sides of each threshold

| Moisture read in | Test weight recorded | Step added to the programme's rate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| above 20.0 percent | below 54.0 pounds | 0.008 |
| above 20.0 percent | 54.0 pounds or more | 0.004 |
| 20.0 percent or below | below 54.0 pounds | none |
| 20.0 percent or below | 54.0 pounds or more | none |

Both thresholds are read strictly: grain read in at exactly 20.0 percent is not above the wet-intake moisture and carries no step at all, and grain weighed in at exactly 54.0 pounds is not below the light-test weight, so wet grain at exactly that weight carries the wet-corn step rather than the deep-dry step.

## Where the two readings are found

Both are recorded against the member's own delivery into storage in the grain ledger kept under Grain Marketing Contracts: the moisture percentage and the test weight in pounds taken on the most recent such delivery.

## Worked steps, on a hypothetical rate

Take a programme whose posted rate is 0.0470 for each point on each bushel.

**Read in at 21.6 percent, weighed in at 51.3 pounds.** Wet and light together, so the deep-dry step of 0.008 is added to the posted rate.

**Read in at 21.6 percent, weighed in at 55.8 pounds.** Wet but not light, so the wet-corn step of 0.004 is added.

**Read in at 18.9 percent, weighed in at 51.0 pounds.** Not above the wet-intake moisture, so no step is added for the state the grain came in at, light though it was.
